note: Production run 10: the Nau da Índia and the galleon (plain sails; crosses to follow on the picked ones), and harbours for the ports history opens: Mpinda, São Tomé, São Brás, Porto Seguro, Calicut.

items.prompt: A photorealistic photograph of a real full-size Portuguese nau da Índia (great carrack) of about 1510, about 40 metres long, much bigger and taller than an ordinary nau: a very high rounded hull with four decks, a towering multi-storey sterncastle and a tall forecastle overhanging the bow, a row of small closed gunports low along the hull, square sails on the foremast and mainmast with topsails above them, a lateen mizzen and a small lateen bonaventure mast at the stern, a spritsail under the bowsprit, plain undyed sails. Same kind of ship as the reference photo but larger, taller and heavier. A working East Indiaman of the Carreira da Índia, no gilding, not a galleon, not a pirate ship. Seen exactly side-on, bow pointing right, warm late afternoon light from the right. Weathered linen sails, hemp rigging, dark tarred planking. Not a model: a real ship. She is isolated on a solid, flat, evenly lit chroma-key green background (#00b140) filling everything around her, including below the hull: no sea, no sky, no shadow, no floor, no stand, no cradle. The whole ship from the mastheads to the keel in frame, with a margin all round.

A photorealistic still from a big-budget historical film set in 1485, natural light, shot on a 35mm lens, meticulous period detail. The mouth of the great Congo river in Central Africa: a vast brown river many miles wide pouring into the sea, low banks of tall grass and mangrove, a village of rectangular houses of palm-leaf matting under thatched roofs among oil palms and baobabs, a stone pillar topped with a cross standing on a low point, large dugout canoes, humid haze, warm afternoon light. Camera on the water about 250 to 300 metres from the shore, at water level, horizon exactly at mid-height. The lower half of the frame is calm open water with soft ripples and long reflections, completely empty in the near water and across the left two-thirds: no boats, no quay, no posts, no rocks, nothing close to the camera. The shore and everything on it sit in the middle distance, small with distance. Nothing later than 1485 anywhere: no cars, street lamps, power lines, tyres, concrete, plastic, glass windows, motorboats, ferries, modern clothing, tall townhouse facades, Baroque spires. No text, no border, no watermark.
